text:
alex: Hey - trying to lock down a canonical benchmark checklist. We're seeing different teams report TTFT/TPOT numbers that aren't comparable. Can we agree on an apples-to-apples protocol?

jordan: +1. we need strict rules for: kernel pins, batching distribution, kv-cache warmup, client-side vs server-side timing.

priya: Proposal: 1) Replay harness only for apples-to-apples (same req seq, same timestamps). 2) Synthetic is allowed for stress but must be labeled. 3) Measure TTFT and TPOT with client-observed times and server trace for debug.

chris: Concrete defs I use: TTFT = time from server receive (ingress timestamp) to first byte emitted to client. TPOT = mean per-output-token latency measured across stream (exclude initial decode jitter). p95/p99 reported for both. Goodput = tokens emitted / GPU-seconds. QPS = completed requests / wall-second.

mia: Add KV cache metrics: hit-rate over rolling window, cold-start vs steady-state. Bench should run a 10k-request warmup, then the measurement window (30m or X tokens).

alex: Sounds good. Two details: a) kernel selection must be reproducible - include commit hash + kernel matrix used. b) batch distribution: capture empirical batch-size histogram from production for replay; synthetic should sample that histogram.

jordan: also: include network jitter modeling when comparing hosted vs dedicated. we should surface both client-observed and server-observed TTFT. store both.

priya: Example harness snippet for reproducibility:
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-small-v1",
  "kernel_commit": "a1b2c3d4",
  "kv_cache": "enabled",
  "replay_trace": "trace-2026-03-01-agg.json",
  "batch_histogram_file": "batch-hist-prod-202602.json",
  "warmup_requests": 10000,
  "measurement_seconds": 1800
}
```

chris: FYI we hit a regression last week after an auto-kernel swap: TTFT p95 jumped 18% for short-seq requests. Profiling showed expensive memcpy in kernel B. Patch: pinned kernel selector for short seqs until we fix the memcpy.

mia: Can we add a KV-cache hot/cold split in reports? e.g. report TTFT p95 for cached requests, and for uncached requests separately. That avoids mixing two distributions.

bench-bot: Perf run 1972104567-report: model=gpt-small-v1, kernel=a1b2c3d4, kv=on, warmup=10k, measurement=1800s. TTFT p50/p95/p99 = 12ms / 48ms / 120ms. TPOT median=2.1ms. Goodput=1.3M tokens / GPU-hour. Full artifacts: s3://redwood-bench/1972104567/

alex: Great. Next steps: codify the checklist as a test in bench-harness repo, add a validator that enforces kernel commit fields + batch histogram present, and update docs with the exact formulas for TTFT/TPOT/goodput. I'll start a PR.

priya: I'll add an example replay trace and a small README describing how to generate production-like batch histograms.

jordan: And I'll add a dashboard showing cached vs uncached TTFT p95 over time so we can catch regressions quickly.

chris: If anyone hits a kernel-induced regression, @chris assign me and I'll triage fast.

mia: agreed. Also add a field for RNG seed for synthetic runs so results are reproducible.

alex: Thanks all. I'll post the PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
